usage: tunnel set [-h] [--base BASE] [--json] [-d JSON] [--script FILE]
                  [--target URL] [--replay] [--strategy {match,sequence,last}]
                  [--session NAME] [--merge JSON] [-H 'Name: value']
                  [--content-type TYPE] [--fault {none,hang,garbage,close}]
                  [--fault-seconds SECONDS]
                  [--mode {json,passthrough,script,replay}] [--status STATUS]
                  [--delay SECONDS] [--desc DESC] [--enable] [--disable]
                  method path

positional arguments:
  method                HTTP method, e.g. GET
  path                  a path (/api/feed) or a host and path
                        (api.example.com/api/feed); * is a wildcard in both

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --base BASE           where the admin API answers (default
                        http://127.0.0.1:8000)
  --json                print raw JSON, errors included, for piping into jq
  -d, --data JSON       the JSON to answer with: literal, or @file
  --script FILE         a JavaScript or TypeScript file defining handler(ctx),
                        run per request
  --target URL          pass through to this base URL or full URL instead of
                        the request's own origin
  --replay              answer from the recordings instead of the real server
  --strategy {match,sequence,last}
                        which recording replay picks: the one whose query
                        matches (default), the next one in order, or the
                        newest
  --session NAME        pin this endpoint to one recorded session; left out it
                        follows the current session, and --session '' unpins
                        it
  --merge JSON          deep merge this object into the JSON that comes back,
                        in passthrough and replay; literal JSON or @file
  -H, --header 'Name: value'
                        response header, repeatable; these replace the rule's
                        headers rather than adding to them
  --content-type TYPE   override the content-type of the response
  --fault {none,hang,garbage,close}
                        answer with a fault instead: hang until fault_seconds
                        then 504, garbage that does not parse as the JSON it
                        claims, or close the connection with no answer at all
  --fault-seconds SECONDS
                        how long --fault hang holds the request before it
                        answers 504 (default 3600, longer than any client's
                        timeout)
  --mode {json,passthrough,script,replay}
                        set the mode explicitly
  --status STATUS       the status code to answer with
  --delay SECONDS       hold the answer back this long
  --desc DESC           a note, shown by `tunnel ls`
  --enable
  --disable
